headlines.title: Fastenal (FAST) Earnings Put Its Valuation Back In Focus
headlines.summary: Fastenal (FAST) is back in focus after reporting third quarter results that featured higher sales, stronger earnings, and a clear boost from demand tied to AI data center projects. Fastenal shares sit at US$51.91 after slipping 1.56% on a 1-day share price basis. However, the 90-day share price return of 10.40% and year to date gain of 28.

headlines.title: Does AI Data Center Demand Change The Bull Case For Fastenal (FAST)?
headlines.summary: Fastenal reported third quarter 2026 sales of US$2,463.3 million and net income of US$401.6 million, with earnings per share of US$0.35 from continuing operations. AI driven data center demand played a material role in supporting Fastenal's recent earnings performance. This highlights how newer technology end markets are influencing this industrial distributor's order flow.

headlines.title: Fastenal (FAST) Stock Looks Rich Even After Stronger Earnings
headlines.summary: Fastenal has delivered a strong run in recent years, and the question now is whether the current share price properly reflects what its earnings justify. With the stock around US$51.91, investors are asking how much of the recent profitability story is already embedded in that valuation. Over the past 5 years the stock has returned about 104.1%. This puts real focus on whether the earnings stream today can support that kind of rerating.

headlines.title: IBD Stock Of The Day: From Nuts And Bolts To Artificial Intelligence
headlines.summary: Q3 Fastenal earnings jumped 21%, the best gain in years, aided by AI data center demand. The Stock Of The Day is just below a buy point.

headlines.title: Fastenal vs. Grainger vs. MSC Industrial: Which Dividend Wins for Retirement?
headlines.summary: Fastenal, Grainger, and MSC Industrial all profit from the same factory supply chain, but the dividend each pays comes with a very different tradeoff between yield, safety, and growth potential.

description: Fastenal Company, together with its subsidiaries, engages in the wholesale distribution of industrial and construction supplies in the United States, Canada, Mexico, and internationally. It offers fasteners, and related industrial and construction supplies under the Fastenal name. The company's fastener products include threaded fasteners, bolts, nuts, screws, studs, and related washers that are used in manufactured products and construction projects, as well as in the maintenance and repair of machines. It offers miscellaneous supplies and hardware, including pins, machinery keys, concrete anchors, metal framing systems, wire ropes, strut products, rivets, and related accessories. The company serves the manufacturing market comprising original equipment manufacturers; maintenance, repair, and operations customers; non-residential construction market; farmers, truckers, railroads, mining companies, schools, and retail trades; and oil exploration, production, and refinement companies, as well as federal, state, and local governmental entities. Fastenal Company was founded in 1967 and is headquartered in Winona, Minnesota.
